GBP.note: Sterling rebounded to around $1.324 as easing oil prices and stabilising global bond markets boosted risk appetite, Brent retreating after Trump ruled out attacking Iran before the midterms. BoE chief economist Huw Pill stressed the need to keep inflation under control and MPC member Megan Greene warned UK wage growth could reach ~3.5% in 2027, potentially requiring further hikes; markets were pricing a BoE hike for November.

NZD.note: No driver given for the session itself. The page notes the kiwi was down 0.1% on the week and, if held to the close, that would mark its SEVENTH CONSECUTIVE WEEKLY DECLINE.

CAD.note: Canada September employment MISSED a +9.2K expectation with a 68.3K DECLINE; following August's -41.7K the two-month loss reaches 110K. USDCAD jumped from ~1.4232 before the report to ~1.4293 after, partly retraced, with the loonie still under pressure. The dollar finished strongest against CAD and JPY, about +0.25% each.

AUD.note: The dollar finished mixed and was WEAKEST AGAINST THE AUSTRALIAN DOLLAR on the session.

USD.note: Preliminary October University of Michigan consumer sentiment fell to 46.3 from 48.1, below the 47.8 estimate. Treasury curve flattened as consumers reported rising inflation expectations; all five major indices finished higher.

Treasury yields steady as a volatile week closed: 10y at 5.244%, 30y down under 1bp to 5.60%, 2y UP more than 3bp to 4.789%. The 10y and 30y each hit their highest since 2002 earlier in the week. CME FedWatch prices an 18% chance of an October hike and 82% for December.
